verses.text: A few days later, Jesus came back to Capernaum. Word got around that he was home.
People piled in until the whole place was packed—no room left, not even by the doorway. Jesus was sharing God’s message with them.
Then four people showed up carrying a man who couldn’t walk.
The crowd blocked every way in, so they opened up the roof above Jesus. Once they’d made a gap, they lowered the mat the man was lying on. Talk about committed friends. 🧗
Jesus saw their faith and told the man, “Son, your sins are forgiven.”
Some legal teachers were sitting there, quietly debating it in their hearts:
“Why is he talking like that? That’s blasphemy! Who can forgive sins except God alone?”
Jesus immediately knew in his spirit what they were thinking, so he said, “Why are you running these thoughts through your hearts?
“Which is easier: telling this man who can’t walk, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or saying, ‘Get up, pick up your mat, and walk’?”
“But so you’ll know the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—then he said to the man who couldn’t walk—
“I’m telling you: get up, pick up your mat, and go home.”
The man got up, picked up his mat, and walked out in front of everybody. They were all amazed and praised God: “We’ve never seen anything like this!” 🔥
Jesus went back out beside the sea. The whole crowd came to him, and he taught them.
As he walked along, he saw Levi son of Alphaeus sitting at the tax booth. Jesus said, “Follow me.” Levi got up and followed him.
Later, Jesus was eating at Levi’s house. Lots of tax collectors and people known as sinners were eating with Jesus and his disciples—there were plenty of them following him.
When the legal teachers from the Pharisee group saw Jesus eating with sinners and tax collectors, they asked his disciples, “Why’s he eating with those tax collectors and sinners?”
Jesus heard them and said, “Healthy people don’t need a doctor; sick people do. I didn’t come to call people who think they’re righteous. I came to call sinners to turn back to God.”
John’s disciples and the Pharisees were fasting. Some people asked Jesus, “Why are John’s disciples and the Pharisees’ disciples fasting, while your disciples aren’t?”
Jesus said, “Can the groom’s friends fast while the groom is still with them? While he’s there with them, fasting doesn’t fit.
“But the time will come when the groom is taken away from them. Then, on that day, they’ll fast.”
“Nobody sews a patch of new, unshrunk cloth onto an old garment. The new patch will pull away from the old, and the tear will get worse.
“And nobody pours new wine into old wineskins. The wine will burst the skins, and both the wine and the skins will be ruined. New wine goes in new wineskins.”
One Sabbath, Jesus was walking through the grain fields. As they went, his disciples started picking heads of grain.
The Pharisees said to him, “Look at that! Why are they doing what isn’t allowed on the Sabbath?”
Jesus replied, “Haven’t you read what David did when he and his companions were hungry and had nothing to eat?
“He went into God’s house while Abiathar was high priest and ate the sacred bread—which only priests were allowed to eat—and shared it with the people with him.”
Then Jesus told them, “The Sabbath was made to help people; people weren’t made to serve the Sabbath.
“So the Son of Man is Lord even over the Sabbath.”
